To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fernhollow Photo is a real business now (!!)

I have some news, and I wanted to put it all here before Thanksgiving, mostly because if I try to explain everything at Ruthie’s after the turkey I’m going to get emotional and forget the actual business parts.

So: I’m going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business!! Fernhollow Photo LLC, to be precise, which still sounds like somebody else’s company when I say it out loud. I filed the LLC paperwork on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in my car outside a Fred Meyer. Extremely glamorous. Very CEO of me. I cried a little in the parking lot, and then Sam made me a cake that said FERNHOLOW. One L short, but full of frosting and support. We ate it anyway. Honestly it tasted completely correct.

Some of you already know that Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6. I had shot for her for four years, which is hard to believe when I look back at how little I knew when I started. She basically taught me everything: the photography, the work, how to be calm when a wedding day is not calm, how to take care of people while also doing the job. She trusted me with her couples long before I felt ready, and she’s been telling me I could do this for longer than I’ve believed her.

Marisol, if you read this: thank you. I wouldn’t be doing this without you, and I mean that. Six of my 2027 bookings came to me through your referrals, and I don’t take that trust lightly.

The timing has made this feel sudden from the outside, I know. But the business itself is not a sudden decision, and I’m not being reckless. I’ve been planning this in my head for about two years, thinking through what I’d need, what I’d do differently, what I could handle, and whether I could actually make a living at it. Rosebud Lane closing changed when I had to make the leap. It didn’t create the idea out of nowhere.

And yes, it’s scary. I’m not going to pretend I’m just breezing around being Fearless Business Woman. There are moments when I look at my calendar and think, oh no, somebody has put me in charge. But scary and unprepared are not the same thing, and I have a plan.

Here are the actual numbers, because I know this family, and I know vague excitement only gets me so far before the questions start. I already have fourteen weddings booked for 2027. Six are referrals from Marisol, and eight found me on my own. Contracts are signed and deposits are in. My website went live November 1. For the bigger weddings, Jae will second-shoot with me, paid per wedding, so I won’t be attempting to cover an entire wedding by cloning myself. June is currently my busiest month, and I’m booked as far out as Wallowa Lake in September, which feels pretty incredible to say.

Dad, this next part is specifically for you: health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. You can relax and enjoy your turkey.

The first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken. They’re getting married at Timberline on June 12, and they found me because of the couple pictures I took at Multnomah Falls. Not through a referral, not because somebody handed them my name. They saw the photos, liked my work, and chose me. I don’t think I can explain what that felt like without sounding ridiculous, so I’ll just say there may have been more parking-lot-adjacent emotions. Dahlia and Ken, thank you for being the people who made this feel real in a completely new way.

As for the name, that part goes back a lot further than the LLC paperwork. Fernhollow comes from the fern hollow trail behind Grandma’s old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with her Pentax. I didn’t know what I was doing yet. I just knew that I loved looking for something, finding the frame, and getting to keep a little piece of it afterward. So much of what I do now still feels like that, just with better backup batteries and significantly more timelines.

Grandma, the name is for you. You gave me the camera, and that trail was the beginning of all of this, even if neither of us knew it at the time. I hope you like seeing a little bit of that place in the name every time I use it. I think about it a lot.

I’m sad about Rosebud Lane. I loved those years, and I’m always going to be proud of the work I did there. But I’m also really excited about what comes next. I get to build something that’s mine, keep doing the work I love, and meet people at these huge, happy moments in their lives. Sometimes they let me stand close enough to cry behind the camera during the toasts. Occupational hazard.

One more thing: would anybody like free family pictures at Thanksgiving? I’m bringing my camera to Ruthie’s. We can do a big group picture, smaller family ones, kids running around, whatever people want. No charge, no sales pitch, nobody has to order a canvas the size of the dining room table. Uncle Greg, I promise to be efficient, or at least more efficient than Christmas. Comment here or tell me on the day and we’ll make it happen.

So that’s the news. Fernhollow Photo. Fourteen weddings. One properly insured photographer. One supportive spouse who should maybe not be in charge of lettering, but is very good at cake.

Love you all. I’m nervous, I’m excited, and I’m ready. See you at Ruthie’s—I’ll be the one with the rolls, the cranberry thing, and approximately too much camera equipment.
